title: Bible Verses for Guidance When You Have a Hard Decision | Prayed
headline: Bible verses for a hard decision, and a way to pray one through
dek: Fourteen verses on guidance, arranged as a way of praying through a decision over a few weeks rather than a night: asking, listening, and then choosing.
desc: Fourteen Bible verses for guidance and hard decisions from the World English Bible, arranged as a way to pray a decision through over weeks: asking for wisdom, listening, and then choosing without fear. With a prayer to write for each stage.
card: Fourteen verses on guidance, arranged as a way of praying through a decision over weeks: asking, listening, choosing.
about: Bible verses for guidance and decisions
intro: Should we take the job? Move closer to her parents? Leave the church? Big decisions are rarely settled in one prayer, and the people who tell you they got a clear answer on the first night are usually leaving out the six weeks before it.

The verses below are quoted word for word from the World English Bible and arranged as a way of praying a decision through, in three movements: asking, listening, and choosing. It is not a method that guarantees an answer. It is a way to keep praying about the same thing for long enough that an answer has room to arrive, and to have a record of what you asked when it does.
One suggestion before you start. Date your first prayer about the decision. Most guidance in hindsight looks like a series of small nudges, and you only see the series if you kept the earlier ones.

paras: The first movement is simply asking, plainly, for wisdom. Scripture treats this as a request God is glad to receive, which takes some pressure off. You are not trying to guess the right answer. You are asking to be taught.

verses.note: Liberally and without reproach. You will not be scolded for not knowing. Ask.
Show me, teach me, guide me. Three verbs, and then I wait for you all day long. The waiting is part of the asking.
A morning prayer. Cause me to know the way. Pray it at the start of each day the decision is open.
A lamp, not a floodlight. Enough light for the next step is what is promised, and it is usually what you get.

sections.pray: We have to decide about the move by the end of the month and we do not know. I am asking for wisdom because you said you give it. Show me the way, one step's worth of light at a time. I will keep asking every morning until it is clear.

paras: The middle movement is the uncomfortable one. You have asked. Now you keep the question open without forcing it closed. These verses are about the voice behind you and the Spirit who guides, and about not leaning on the version of the answer you have already decided you want.

verses.note: Lean is the honest word. The temptation in a decision is to trust your own understanding because it is the only thing that feels solid. The verse asks you to acknowledge him in the middle of the not-knowing.
A voice behind you, not ahead. Guidance in this picture often comes after you have taken the step, confirming it, rather than before.
With my eye on you. You are being watched over while you decide, not graded on the result.
The Spirit guides into truth. It is not a promise of a map. It is a promise of a guide.

sections.pray: I notice I have already decided what I want the answer to be. I am putting that down. Keep my ears open for the voice behind me. If this is the wrong way, make it clear before I turn.

paras: At some point the decision has to be made, usually before you feel certain. These verses are for that day. They say something surprising: that you can plan and choose, and that God directs the steps anyway. The pressure to get it perfectly right is not one scripture puts on you.

verses.note: Both halves are true. You plan the course. He directs the steps. Choosing is not a failure of faith.
Established. Once you have chosen in good faith, the step is his to hold up.
Continually. Guidance does not stop at the decision. If you choose wrong, you will still be guided, from wherever you end up.
Often quoted, rarely in context. It was written to exiles who would stay in exile for seventy years. The hope and future are real. The timeline is God's.

sections.pray: We are going to say yes to the job. I have asked, I have waited, I have listened as well as I know how, and this is where the light seems to point. Direct our steps from here. If I have chosen wrong, guide us anyway.

closing_h2: Keep the prayers on both sides of the decision
closing: The strangest thing about praying through a decision is how quickly you forget what you prayed once it is made. A year in, the move feels inevitable, or regrettable, and the weeks of asking are gone. So is the evidence of the small answers along the way.

Prayed brings each written prayer back to you at three days, a week, a month and a year, so the prayer from the first morning of the asking is placed in front of you again once you are living inside the answer. You can mark it answered, or ongoing, and the whole sequence stays together. Nothing you write leaves your phone.
Write the first prayer about the decision today, before you know how it ends. That is the only time you can.
